lines.text: Where does your breath go? Not into a bag. Into these.
lines.phonemes: wˌeə dˈʌz jɔː bɹˈɛθ ɡˈəʊ? nˌɒt ˌɪntʊ ɐ bˈaɡ. ˌɪntʊ ðˈiːz.

lines.text: Below your windpipe, the airways fork again and again, about twenty-three times. At the tips hang tiny air pockets, half a billion of them, each a fifth of a millimetre.
lines.phonemes: bɪlˌəʊ jɔː wˈɪndpaɪp, ðɪ ˈeəweɪz fˈɔːk ɐɡˈɛn and ɐɡˈɛn, ɐbˌaʊt twˈɛntiθɹˈiː tˈaɪmz. at ðə tˈɪps hˈaŋ tˈaɪni ˈeə pˈɒkɪts, hˈɑːf ɐ bˈɪliən ɒv ðˌɛm, ˈiːtʃ ɐ fˈɪfθ əvə mˈɪlɪmˌiːtə.

lines.text: For centuries, physicians taught the lung was clotted blood, there to cool the heart. In sixteen sixty-one, Marcello Malpighi put an animal's lung under a microscope: bubbles.
lines.phonemes: fɔː sˈɛntʃəɹiz, fɪzˈɪʃənz tˈɔːt ðə lˈʌŋ wɒz klˈɒtɪd blˈʌd, ðeə tə kˈuːl ðə hˈɑːt. ɪn sˈɪkstiːn sˈɪkstiwˌɒn, mɑːtʃˈɛləʊ malpˈiːɡi pˌʊt ɐn ˈanɪməlz lˈʌŋ ˌʌndəɹ ɐ mˈaɪkɹəskˌəʊp: bˈʌbəlz.

lines.text: Each pocket is wrapped in tiny blood vessels. In places, the wall between air and blood is far thinner than a red cell. Oxygen just slips across, no pump needed. Thicken that wall, and breathing gets harder.
lines.phonemes: ˈiːtʃ pˈɒkɪt ɪz ɹˈapt ɪn tˈaɪni blˈʌd vˈɛsəlz. ɪn plˈeɪsɪz, ðə wˈɔːl bɪtwˌiːn ˈeə and blˈʌd ɪz fˈɑː θˈɪnə ðˌanə ɹˈɛd sˈɛl. ˈɒksɪdʒən dʒˈʌst slˈɪps əkɹˈɒs, nˈəʊ pˈʌmp nˈiːdɪd. θˈɪkən ðat wˈɔːl, and bɹˈiːðɪŋ ɡˈɛts hˈɑːdə.

lines.text: Spread every pocket out flat, and they'd cover about a quarter of a tennis court. All of that, folded up inside your chest.
lines.phonemes: spɹˈɛd ˈɛvɹɪ pˈɒkɪt ˈaʊt flˈat, and ðeɪd kˈʌvəɹ ɐbˌaʊt ɐ kwˈɔːtəɹ əvə tˈɛnɪs kˈɔːt. ˈɔːl ɒv ðˈat, fˈəʊldɪd ˌʌp ɪnsˈaɪd jɔː tʃˈɛst.

lines.text: So your lungs aren't a bag. They're a sponge that spreads air thin.
lines.phonemes: sˌəʊ jɔː lˈʌŋz ˌɑːnt ɐ bˈaɡ. ðeɪəɹ ɐ spˈʌndʒ ðat spɹˈɛdz ˈeə θˈɪn.

lines.text: Meanwhile, as you watched, air went in and out of you. About six litres of it.
lines.phonemes: mˈiːnwaɪl, az juː wˈɒtʃt, ˈeə wˈɛnt ɪn and ˌaʊtəv juː. ɐbˌaʊt sˈɪks lˈiːtəz ɒv ɪt.

lines.text: Next: a cell that leaves your blood. It squeezes through a wall.
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: ɐ sˈɛl ðat lˈiːvz jɔː blˈʌd. ɪt skwˈiːzɪz θɹuː ɐ wˈɔːl.
